title: Layer Edelstein Effect
authors: Binchang Zhou, Pan Zhou, Baoru Pan, Yuzhong Hu, Songmin Liu, Lizhong Sun
abstract: Electrical control of magnetism represents a fundamental route toward next-generation spintronic functionalities. In this Letter, we introduce a universal current-induced spin phenomenon in bilayer systems, termed the layer Edelstein effect (LEE), which serves as the natural counterpart of the layer Hall effect in real space. It is defined by the emergence of layer-resolved spin magnetizations with opposite components on the top and bottom layers, driven by an in-plane charge current and controllable by an external electric field. We establish the general existence of the LEE using a minimal bilayer $k \cdot p$ theory. By combining symmetry analysis with a general bilayer stacking framework, we derive a model-independent symmetry criterion demonstrating that the LEE is generically allowed in a broad class of nonmagnetic bilayer stacking systems. We further show that the LEE admits two universal manifestations: explicit layer-opposite spin magnetization components mandated directly by symmetry, and components become activated upon symmetry reduction by external electric fields. First-principles calculations on stacked bilayer MoSSe, MoTe$_2$ and WTe$_2$ confirm the predicted effect and illustrate their experimental feasibility. Our work establishes the LEE as a generic symmetry-governed response of bilayer systems, providing a unified conceptual framework for electrically generating and manipulating layer-resolved spin polarization.
summary: This work introduces the Layer Edelstein Effect (LEE), a symmetry-protected mechanism generating opposite layer-resolved spin magnetizations in bilayer systems using an in-plane current. By developing model-independent symmetry criteria, the authors prove LEE is generic for many nonmagnetic bilayers and confirm its feasibility on materials like MoSSe via first-principles calculations.
main_problem: The paper introduces and establishes the 'layer Edelstein effect' (LEE), a universal current-induced spin phenomenon in bilayer systems, as a counterpart to the layer Hall effect.
main_result: The LEE is shown to be a generic, symmetry-governed response realizable in a wide class of nonmagnetic bilayer stackings. It manifests through layer-resolved spin magnetizations with opposite components on top and bottom layers.
method: The authors combine symmetry analysis with a general bilayer k.p theory framework to derive model-independent criteria for LEE existence.
model_or_system: The study focuses on nonmagnetic bilayer systems, such as stacked MoSSe, MoTe2, and WTe2. The theoretical analysis uses group theory based on stacking operators ($\hat{P}$) applied to a minimal bilayer k.p Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Layer-resolved spin magnetizations with opposite components; the symmetry criteria for LEE realization ($\chi_{xy}$ vs $\chi_{yx}$).
important_parameters: In-plane charge current density ($\mathbf{j}_A$) and external electric field ($\mathbf{E}$); bilayer stacking symmetry (point group).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that interlayer tunneling can be suppressed by weak coupling, symmetry selection rules, and electric-field detuning.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates LEE using the stacking operator; Figure 2 shows how breaking inversion symmetry via E leads to measurable spin responses ($\chi_{xy}$ vs $\chi_{yx}$).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the concept of LEE, then establishes its general existence and symmetry criteria using group theory on bilayer systems. It details two universal manifestations (symmetry-mandated vs. field-activated) before confirming predictions via first-principles calculations on specific TMD bilayers.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, understanding how symmetries dictate emergent spin responses in layered materials is crucial for designing quantum devices that rely on controlled spin-orbit coupling effects.
